official.deadline_note: SUSS publishes no standalone scholarship deadline: awards follow each programme's admissions cycle, with PhD applications due by 28 February for the July semester and by 31 August for the January semester.
official.application_cycle: July 2026 semester onwards (MOE subsidy and SUSS Research Scholarship both available from the July 2026 intake); Jan 2027 intake closed 31 August 2026
official.status_note: All applications for the Jan 2027 intake had to be submitted and complete by 31 August 2026; incomplete applications as of that date are not considered for the scholarship. The next window is the July semester, with applications due by 28 February 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: For part-time students, the scholarship covers the tuition fee (excludes annual miscellaneous fees). For full-time students, the scholarship covers the tuition fees (excludes annual miscellaneous fees) and a monthly stipend.
benefits: Full-time: tuition fees (excluding annual miscellaneous fees) plus a monthly stipend
Part-time: tuition fee only (excluding annual miscellaneous fees)
Monthly stipend for PhD: S$4,300 Singapore Citizen, S$3,900 Permanent Resident, S$3,500 International Student
Monthly stipend for Master of Applied Research in Social Sciences: S$3,800 Singapore Citizen, S$3,000 Permanent Resident, S$2,900 International Student
CPF is given on top of the stipend amounts for Singapore Citizens
International Students become eligible for the government tuition subsidy only if awarded this scholarship
eligibility: Applicant seeking admission to one of the three SUSS postgraduate programmes: Doctor of Philosophy, Doctor of Philosophy (Gerontology), or Master of Applied Research in Social Sciences
At least a 2nd Upper Class Honours Degree from a reputable university or equivalent qualifications
Demonstrated academic excellence in social sciences
Research topics should relate to SUSS's Research Focus
Research proposals relevant to the social services sector, with a clearly identified industry collaborator and likely cash and/or in-kind industry support, are prioritised
requirements: Indicate interest in the SUSS Research Scholarship in the Research Proposal Template application form
Submit the PhD application by the programme deadline and have it complete by that date
International students on scholarship must fulfil the Graduate Assistantship Programme (GAP) requirement
Scholarship recipients must maintain a cumulative grade point average (CGPA) of at least 3.8 in every semester
documents: Research Proposal Template application form indicating interest in the SUSS Research Scholarship
Proposed topic or area of research and identified potential supervisor (if any)
Evidence of at least a 2nd Upper Class Honours Degree or equivalent qualifications
selection_criteria: Merit basis during the admissions interview of the three eligible programmes
Identification and nomination of potential applicants as part of the interview process
Panel interview for nominated applicants, notified by email
Priority for proposals relevant to the social services sector with an identified industry collaborator and likely cash or in-kind support
The decision of the SUSS Student Awards Committee is final and binding; no reasons are given and no appeals are entertained
coverage: Tuition fees excluding annual miscellaneous fees for full-time students
Monthly stipend for full-time students, by citizenship and programme
Tuition fee only excluding annual miscellaneous fees for part-time students
CPF contributions on top of the stipend for Singapore Citizens
application_method: Apply for admission to one of the three eligible SUSS postgraduate programmes
Submit the application and have it complete by the programme deadline (28 February for July semester, 31 August for January semester)
Indicate interest in the SUSS Research Scholarship in the Research Proposal Template application form
Be evaluated on merit during the admissions interview and, if nominated, attend the panel interview by email invitation
official.application_route: Apply through the SUSS graduate programme application, flag interest in the scholarship inside the Research Proposal Template, then wait for nomination from the admissions interview.
official.study_mode: Full-time or part-time (part-time receives tuition fee coverage only)
official.citizenship_residency: Open to Singapore Citizens, Singapore Permanent Residents and International Students
official.international_eligibility: International students are eligible. They qualify for the government tuition subsidy only if awarded this scholarship, must fulfil the Graduate Assistantship Programme (GAP) requirement, and receive no remuneration for hours clocked under the GAP.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Proposed research must align with SUSS's Research Focus and the expertise of SUSS faculty; social services sector proposals with an identified industry collaborator are prioritised.
official.research_requirement: A proposed topic or area of research stated in the Research Proposal Template, with an identified potential supervisor where possible, is part of the application.
official.duration: A maximum of four (4) years for PhD programmes and two (2) years for the master programme
official.description: SUSS states that the SUSS Research Scholarship aims to support applicants who have demonstrated academic excellence in social sciences and whose proposed research aligns with the research focus of the Singapore University of Social Sciences and the expertise of its faculty.
official.program_type: Research scholarship for full-time and part-time PhD, PhD (Gerontology) and Master of Applied Research in Social Sciences

not_confirmed: amount of the excluded annual miscellaneous fees
verification.notes: The SUSS scholarship page returned HTTP 403 to four direct fetch attempts, so values were taken from SUSS's own published content on suss.edu.sg (the scholarship page, the MOE subsidies and Research Scholarship news article dated 7 January 2026, and the PhD programme page); the stipend table, tenure and eligibility text are identical across all three. English-language requirements are set by each programme's admission criteria, not by the scholarship page.

applicant_utility.summary: This award is not something you apply for directly: you apply to one of the three SUSS research programmes, flag your interest inside the Research Proposal Template, and get nominated out of your admissions interview. The money is citizenship-banded, so an international full-time PhD recipient receives S$3,500 a month plus tuition (minus miscellaneous fees), while the part-time route waives tuition only and pays nothing toward living costs. Because nomination happens at the interview, a late or incomplete application is fatal - the January 2027 window shut on 31 August 2026 and the next one closes 28 February 2027 for the July intake.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Social science researchers holding at least 2nd Upper Class Honours who can build a topic around SUSS's Research Focus and, ideally, a named social-services industry partner.
application_readiness_checklist: Pick the programme first (PhD, PhD Gerontology or MRESS) - the scholarship cannot be decoupled from that admission
Draft the research proposal so it maps explicitly onto SUSS's published Research Focus and a named faculty supervisor
Name a social-services industry collaborator and state what cash or in-kind support they would bring, since this is an explicit priority
Tick the scholarship-interest box inside the Research Proposal Template rather than assuming the admissions team will infer it
Have referees send reference letters straight to the graduate admissions address before the deadline
Check your application is complete before the cut-off; an incomplete file on the deadline date is simply not considered
common_rejection_risks: Submitting an incomplete file on the deadline date, which excludes you regardless of merit
Proposing a topic that reads as generic social science rather than a fit with SUSS's stated Research Focus and faculty expertise
Missing the industry-collaborator angle that SUSS says it prioritises
Never reaching the interview stage because the degree-class threshold (2nd Upper Class Honours or equivalent) was not evidenced clearly
Assuming a separate scholarship form exists and waiting for one, when nomination is made from the admissions interview
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Annual miscellaneous fees, living costs for part-time recipients, flights to and from Singapore, and any costs beyond the stipend. International students also carry an unpaid in-service obligation: GAP hours (teaching or lab supervision, research assistant duties, other developmental assignments) must be fulfilled with no remuneration.
document_audit: The Research Proposal Template is the only place scholarship interest is captured - a missing tick there is the single easiest way to lose the award
Degree transcripts must evidence at least 2nd Upper Class Honours or equivalent; non-UK grading systems should be accompanied by a clear equivalence explanation
Referees submit letters directly rather than you forwarding them, so allow several weeks of lead time and confirm receipt
The stipend differs by programme and citizenship, so check which band you fall into before budgeting - MRESS international recipients get S$2,900, not the PhD S$3,500
alerts: There are two intake windows, not one: 28 February for the July semester and 31 August for the January semester - miss both and you wait a year
International students must keep a CGPA of at least 3.8 every semester to hold the award, so a weak first semester is a funding problem as well as an academic one
Accepting the government tuition subsidy via this scholarship triggers the GAP obligation, and hours must be finished at least six months before graduation
Do not confuse this with the separate SUSS PhD Scholarship, which also covers miscellaneous fees but is full-time PhD only
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Programme application with research proposal through SUSS Graduate Studies, merit screening at the admissions interview, email invitation to a panel interview for nominees, then a final, non-appealable decision from the Student Awards Committee.
